documents.t: The account-deletion page is up, and its flow has not yet passed a live deletion test. It is a signed-in self-service path that asks you to use the Google account linked to Waylock, confirm that sign-in again and explicitly confirm deletion. Deletion then waits 7 days. Sign-in stops during that wait, and you can cancel on the same page or on Account. Removal comes on or soon after the date shown, in your time zone. The website and in-app paths need verification; an uncertain response does not prove that deletion happened.
documents.s: How would I delete my account after uninstalling the app?

documents.t: In the billing portal Polar hosts. Polar emails you the link. Billing ends when your account is removed. To stop it sooner, cancel it there.

documents.t: For an ordinary product or legal question, email aoneahsan@gmail.com. Account deletion uses the signed-in page, not email. If the page cannot confirm an outcome, check the account status before you submit again. If that check fails too, write to aoneahsan@gmail.com, and the team can tell you whether a deletion was scheduled; email cannot delete an account.

By the Waylock team · Last updated: 7 November 2026 Waylock is intended to let you hold a delivery stop in place, choose a range for a trip stop and decide what to do after a wrong turn. Device proof is still missing. Before treating these as available steps, check the release status.
documents.s: How are Waylock routes meant to work?

documents.t: A stop lock is intended to keep one chosen delivery stop in place while the planner reorders other stops around it, subject to the limits you set. Review the estimated order while stopped, before you set off. Times are estimates.
documents.s: How would I keep a delivery stop in position?

documents.t: The Trip planner is intended to find a matching stop within a range measured along the route from the origin or a previous stop. Check the proposed place and route before guidance. A search can find no match.
documents.s: How would I choose a stop within a distance range?

documents.t: Your chosen route is designed to stay visible as an overlay while the Google Navigation SDK may reroute its own guidance, so you can compare a way back with a new route. Stop before choosing. The exact recovery steps for a failed route calculation still need a device test.
documents.s: What would happen after a wrong turn?

documents.t: None yet. The device test must show the actual stop-lock, Trip planner and route-choice controls before the guide can name steps a driver can follow. It must also show what remains safe after a failed route calculation and how the driver recovers. Until then, check the release status.
documents.s: What steps and recovery can this guide give?

documents.t: By the Waylock team · Last updated: 14 November 2026 A white-label licence puts the Waylock Android app in your drivers' hands under your company's name, logo and colours. The Waylock team builds your copy, runs the services behind it and keeps it updated. You run the deliveries. It suits a courier firm, a dispatch office or a field team that wants stop locks, distance ranges and a locked route without building a maps app first.
documents.s: Running Waylock under your own brand

documents.t: Licence. We host and update your branded copy. The source code stays with us, and other firms can license Waylock too until someone buys it outright. Buyout. You receive the source code and Waylock comes off sale to everyone else. You then pay us a 7% royalty on the gross revenue Waylock earns, for as long as it earns (how the royalty works). The licence price page and the buyout page show the current amounts, read from our licensing service. This guide does not repeat them, so it never shows an old number.

What is delivered From payment to launch Updates and renewals Checking a licence Questions buyers ask Waylock is in Google Play internal testing and is not public yet. A licensed copy is published under the buyer's own developer account.

By the Waylock team · Last updated: 13 November 2026 Waylock sells one platform group: the mobile app. A licence for it covers four things. Your Android build. Your app name, icon and colours, built from the current Waylock release and published under your own Google Play developer account. The services behind it. Sign-in, saved stops and routes, and the map and route requests the app makes, set up for your deployment. Your domain. The account, plans and account-deletion pages your drivers open from the app, served on the domain you name. Updates. New Waylock releases applied to your build for the months included with the licence, then renewals if you want them.
documents.s: What is delivered with a Waylock licence

documents.t: Waylock is a native Android app. An iOS app would be a separate build, delivered on request once you provide or fund an Apple developer account. No iOS version exists today.

The source code comes only with a buyout. Changes made only for your drivers are custom work, quoted separately. Accounts you choose to pay for, such as your domain, your store account and paid services, stay yours.
By the Waylock team · Last updated: 14 November 2026
documents.s: Questions buyers ask about a Waylock licence

documents.t: No. A licence covers your built app and the services we run for it. The code changes hands only with a buyout.
documents.s: Do I get the source code with a licence?

documents.t: Yes, until somebody buys it outright. A buyout ends sales to anyone else, and the buyer pays us a 7% royalty on the gross revenue Waylock earns; licences sold before it keep their terms.
documents.s: Can another firm license Waylock as well?

documents.t: You do, under your own developer account. We prepare the build and the listing with you.
documents.s: Who publishes the app on Google Play?

documents.t: Not today. Waylock is built for Android. An iOS build is delivered on request when you provide or fund an Apple developer account.

The Android app repository, with the Supabase migrations and server functions it runs on, the website repository and the guides repository, plus six months of updates. Google Maps Platform, Google Play, Supabase and payment accounts are opened in your name. The buyout agreement carries a royalty: you pay us 7% of the gross revenue Waylock earns, not counting sales tax or VAT collected. It is paid each quarter with a revenue statement, for as long as Waylock earns revenue, and it is still owed after you sell Waylock on. The licence terms set it out.
documents.s: What does a buyout hand over?

documents.t: Yes, as separate paid work. Describe it on the custom work page and we reply with questions or a written quote.
documents.s: Can you change Waylock just for my drivers?

documents.t: The licence terms explain the licence in plain words. The Terms of Service are the binding version and cover payments.

By the Waylock team · Last updated: 14 November 2026 You pay by bank transfer to our Wise account from the payment page, and send us the transfer reference. Access starts when we have confirmed the transfer, not when you return to the website from the payment page. The licence email carries your key and certificate.

Branding. We agree your app name, icon, colours and the domain for your drivers' pages by email. Your build. We prepare the Android build and the store listing with you. Your Play listing. You publish the app under your Google Play developer account. Google reviews it on its own schedule. Deployment. We deploy the services and pages on your domain, with your licence file at /.well-known/waylock-white-label-license.json. No launch date is promised here: Play review and your own decisions set the pace. Ask on the custom work page if you need a date agreed in writing.

By the Waylock team · Last updated: 13 November 2026 An update is a new Waylock release applied to your build: fixes, route-control changes and support for newer Android versions. A licence or a buyout includes six months of updates from the day you pay. A renewal of 3, 6 or 12 months extends them. It counts from the later of today and your current end date, so renewing early loses nothing. Without a renewal, your app keeps running on its last version. Renew on the updates page with your licence key and the email on the licence. That page shows each renewal's current price.

documents.t: By the Waylock team · Last updated: 13 November 2026 Every licensed copy carries a licence key, which starts with WAYLOCK-, and serves a licence file at /.well-known/waylock-white-label-license.json. Verification is run by our licensing service.

Enter the key on Verify a licence. The answer is one of: valid, paid but not yet deployed, revoked, no licence with this key, or not a Waylock key. A valid licence shows the company it is licensed to, its domains, the issue date and the date its updates run until. It never shows an email or a price.

Choose Domain on the same page and enter the address without https://. Our licensing service fetches that domain's licence file and checks the key it names. It reports whether the domain holds a valid licence, names a different domain, has no file, or could not be reached.

A licensed copy checks its own key once each time it starts. If the licence is revoked or does not cover the address it runs on, the app shows a notice and pauses. Nothing saved is deleted. A network failure never pauses the app; it checks again on the next start.
